cheng_li: Quick heads-up — ran the monthly perf sweep on v0.9.3 and hit a regression on the fused-attn path when we enable fused RoPE + rotary scaling. Baseline (no fused-rope) tokens/sec: 18.2k, with fused-rope + rotary_scale=1.5 tokens/sec: 12.1k. p95 latency jumped from 72ms -> 140ms. Repro steps below.

maria_g: Oof. Can you paste the exact command/config you used? seq lengths and batching heuristics matter a lot here.

cheng_li: Repro command + minimal config: 
```
# runner
./perf_runner --model rtd-16b-q --kernel-selection auto --attention=paged,fusedflash --fused-rope=true --rotary-scale=1.5 --batching=adaptive --seq-dist="[32,64,128,512]" --kv-page-size=64
```
Quick perf snippet from `nvprof`-style trace (aggregated):
```
kernel,fusedflash_forward,fusedflash_backward,paged_attn,nonfused
ms,45.2,10.3,22.1,18.0
```
Also saw a spike in kernel retries where we fell back to `paged_attn` mid-request (policy logging).

alex_patel: Interesting. My guess: kernel selector currently treats `fused-rope==true` as compatible with fusedflash only if rotary_dim == head_dim. When rotary_scale != 1.0 we do some extra rescaling ops that blow up the kernel prologue and force extra KV shuffles — that can defeat the fused kernel's continuous batching assumptions.

cheng_li: That matches the traces. The fusedflash kernel shows a larger than usual prologue time (20ms) vs the expected ~4-6ms. Patch idea: if fused-rope && rotary_scale != 1.0 then prefer `paged_attn` for seq_len>256 or when kv_page_size>32. Quick pseudocode: 
```
# kernel_selector.py
if fused_rope and rotary_scale != 1.0 and (seq_len>256 or kv_page_size>32):
    prefer = 'paged_attn'
```
This keeps fusedflash for short seqs but avoids the prologue blowup on longer pages.

siva_kumar: +1 to short-term guard. But where are KV cache evictions coming in? I saw reduced cache hit rate in the logs when we used paged_attn with fused-rope enabled (weird). Cheng, any cache stats?

cheng_li: Yeah — KV hit-rate dropped from ~98% -> ~84% under the failing config. Hypothesis: when kernel selection flips mid-batch we accidentally rebase page offsets and end up duplicating KV writes, invalidating some older pages. I can reproduce with a micro-trace and `--kv-debug`. Sample: 
```
# kv debug lines
[t=0.12] write page 42 (tokens 8192-8255)
[t=0.13] invalidate page 42
[t=0.15] write page 42 (tokens 8192-8255)  <-- duplicated
```
This looks like a race between `batching->split` and `kernel_route` threads when a kernel fallback is triggered.

maria_g: If it's a race, we should avoid switching kernel mid-batch. Maybe add a kernel-stability window: once a batch starts routing to a kernel we lock that kernel for the batch lifetime. Also we should ensure KV page writes are idempotent with a page-version tag.

alex_patel: Agreed. Two-pronged: (1) short term heuristic in kernel selector (cheng's patch) to avoid pathological prologues, (2) longer-term: atomic page writes or versioned pages + a kernel affinity for in-flight batches. We should also add a perf test that toggles rotary_scale and fused-rope across a seq_len distribution to catch regressions in CI.

cheng_li: I'll open a ticket with repro and a small patch for the selector guard. Also adding a unit that asserts no kernel changes mid-batch in the router. Created INC: https://redwood.internal/issue/ENGML-4721 (assigning to eng-ml).

siva_kumar: +:eyes: Can you dump a flamegraph of the prologue vs main loop? If prologue is big we can look into moving some work to precompilation or fuse the rescale into KV layout transform.

cheng_li: Will do. Quick flame: prologue ~20ms (rotary rescale + layout transpose), main loop ~18ms. If we can absorb rescale into the kv layout transform we might claw back ~12ms.

maria_g: Sounds good. For the ticket add the perf numbers, small repro script, nvprof snippet, and the suggested kernel-selector guard. I'll pair with you on the KV idempotency fix.

buildbot: auto-note: nightly perf sweep detected regression on commit c3d9b4a. See ENGML-4721.

alex_patel: TL;DR action items: 1) cheng: open PR for selector guard + perf tests. 2) cheng + maria: reproduce KV race and add page-versioning. 3) siva: investigate fusing rescale into layout transform. 4) add CI scenario toggling fused-rope + rotary-scale combos.

cheng_li: On it. I'll post PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
